question: A smoker draws on a cigarette. How long does the nicotine in that puff take to reach the brain?
answer: About 10 to 20 seconds. Blood leaving the lungs goes straight to the heart and on to the brain, so each puff lands almost at once; a nicotine patch takes hours to build up. A reward that quick, repeated some 200 times a day by a pack-a-day smoker, gets tied to every cue around it.
move: The faster a reward follows an act, the harder the habit breaks.
ask: Which of my habits pays out so fast that it is hard to resist?
reference: Benowitz, Nicotine addiction, New England Journal of Medicine 362(24), 2010; Benowitz, Hukkanen & Jacob, Nicotine chemistry, metabolism, kinetics and biomarkers, Handbook of Experimental Pharmacology 192, 2009
